operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; id="d-078-soundness-gate-no-claim-bearing-extraction-from-time-anchor-defective-powermetrics-corpora">D-078: Soundness gate — no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. The following spellings are the binding, closed registry for D-078 claim refusals and campaign conditions. Consumers preserve these strings verbatim; an unknown claim/refusal spelling never becomes a pass.</p> <ul> <li>Reducer/analysis claim barriers: <code>nonpositive_window_duration</code>, <code>anchor_energy_envelope_unrecorded</code>, <code>anchor_energy_envelope_exceeds_quarter_metric</code>, <code>instrument_calibration_missing</code>, <code>instrument_calibration_mismatch</code>, and <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li>Floor-extraction refusals: <code>bundle_missing</code>, <code>summary_unreadable</code>, <code>bundle_strict_invalid</code>, <code>bundle_hash_unresolved</code>, <code>bundle_status_not_succeeded</code>, <code>reducer_wire_unknown</code>, <code>idle_method_pair_invalid</code>, <code>metric_missing_or_nonfinite</code>, <code>campaign_member_unattributable</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>, <code>insufficient_members_after_exclusion</code>, plus every applicable reducer barrier above and <code>whole_window_neg8_verdict_missing</code>, <code>whole_window_neg8_verdict_failed</code>, <code>adapter_continuity_evidence_missing</code>, <code>adapter_continuity_failed</code>, <code>cpu_admission_core_missing</code>, and <code>cpu_admission_core_failed</code>.</li> <li>Idle-admission/campaign conditions: <code>cpu_baseline_telemetry_missing</code>, <code>cpu_baseline_telemetry_malformed</code>, <code>cpu_baseline_sample_count_insufficient</code>, <code>cpu_busy_ratio_p95_exceeded</code>, <code>processor_combined_power_w_p95_exceeded</code>, <code>gpu_idle_admission_not_passed</code>, <code>gpu_idle_admission_unknown</code>, <code>adapter_observations_missing</code>, <code>adapter_wattage_unknown</code>, <code>adapter_wattage_discontinuity</code>, <code>adapter_description_changed</code>, <code>adapter_power_source_changed</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_missing</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_reference_invalid</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_rel_delta_exceeded</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_ambiguous_reference</code>, <code>idle_admission_attempt_ledger_invalid</code>, <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>, <code>whole_window_bundle_invalid</code>, <code>whole_window_campaign_membership_unresolved</code>, and <code>whole_window_campaign_membership_ambiguous</code>.</li> <li>Instrument-evidence diagnostics: <code>pulse_detection_incomplete</code>, <code>spurious_plateau_detected</code>, <code>residual_interval_unbounded</code>, <code>not_all_pulses_detected</code>, <code>binding_fields_missing:</code>, <code>pulse_count_below_protocol:</code>, and <code>raw_or_event_hash_missing_or_invalid</code>. These diagnostics can only make <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>; they never directly license a claim.</li> </ul> <p>Governance ruling GOV-02: D-078 supersedes only D-028&#39;s former exception that allowed <code>summary_metrics.json</code> to be rewritten after finalization. Stored summary bytes are now immutable evidence. Post-hoc reduction writes a new, non-clobbering artifact (including the repaired anchor envelope) or refuses; the raw-artifact immutability and pure-reducer portions of D-002/D-028 remain in force. Frozen 0.5.0/0.6.0 numeric semantics remain replayable and are not claim-bearing merely because they can be read.</p> <h3>D-078 additive registry addendum — 2026-07-20: causal-set repair</h3> <p>The closed registry additionally includes floor/whole-window barriers <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_coverage_incomplete</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code>, and <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>no_plateau_interior_intervals</code>, <code>plateau_below_minimum</code>, <code>robust_snr_below_minimum</code>, <code>edge_coverage_missing</code>, <code>model_fit_not_significant</code>, and <code>fitted_shift_exceeds_validation_limit</code>. These additions only refuse or widen uncertainty; none can license a claim.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21: convergence fix wave (lead adjudications)</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the two-round cross-model convergence loop over <code>impl/p0-instrument-repair</code> (round-2 and round-3 fix waves; council log carries the layer accounting). Six rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Additive causal-bound composition.</strong> <code>B_effective = B_bundle + B_fiducial</code> replaces <code>max(B_bundle, B_fiducial)</code>. The bundle-local censored-constraint anchor interval and the instrument&#39;s emission-lag bound sit on disjoint causal links; no containment proof exists, so <code>max()</code> under-composes. <code>B_fiducial</code> itself additively folds in the calibration capture&#39;s own trace-anchor bound. The prior <code>max()</code> text in this log is superseded prospectively; stored summaries are never rewritten.</li> <li><strong>Identity bump, not in-place semantics change.</strong> The additive composition, fiducial protocol_v2 physics (<code>joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2</code> full 2-D branch-and-bound region), and the stricter evidence-admission semantics are minted as reducer <code>0.5.2</code> / AXI <code>0.6.2</code> with <code>configs/calibration/powermetrics_fiducial/protocol_v2.json</code>. <code>0.5.1</code> / <code>0.6.1</code> and <code>protocol_v1.json</code> remain byte-frozen replay arms.</li> <li><strong>Superseded arms are claim-ineligible.</strong> <code>0.5.1</code>/<code>0.6.1</code> summaries refuse claim-bearing use with a registered refusal (superseded max-composition envelope semantics); <code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code> are the sole claim-eligible mints.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions (closing the F11/PENDING exception).</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>token_count_stream_chunk_fallback</code> (renamed from the source-label reuse of <code>stream_chunk_fallback</code>), <code>pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout</code> (pre-workload rollover gate timeout now refuses fail-closed, no artifact minting), and <code>post_window_trace_tail_shorter_than_anchor_bound</code> (reduce-time refusal when the post-window trace tail cannot support the composed anchor bound; collection policy raises the minimum post-window dwell to 1.0 s). These only refuse; none can license a claim.</li> <li><strong>Registry closure is one-way by design.</strong> Every emitted spelling must be registered here; a registered spelling with no current emission site (e.g. <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>) is permitted — unemittable names cannot launder anything.</li> <li><strong>Member-level <code>claim_evidence_flags</code> is an all-leaf union — documented, not changed.</strong> Adjudicated a documentation defect only: the union is fail-safe (it can only over-flag, never over-admit) and gating decisions read the per-metric leaves. Scope documented in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>; no wire rename.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (second): two-edge envelope and confirmation-round rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the first confirmation round over <code>5093355</code> correctly withheld sign-off (fresh Sol xhigh audit; 8 confirmed findings, one P0). Rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Corner-composed two-edge envelope (P0 repair).</strong> The calibration fits independent start-edge and stop-edge emission lags; a single common trace shift under-covers because independent endpoint errors move energy by up to <code>2·P·B_fiducial</code> even when a common shift cancels. The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). New registered method spelling for the 0.5.2/0.6.2 mints; v1/v2 spellings remain replay-read-only.</li> <li><strong>In-place revision of the unreleased mints.</strong> Reducer 0.5.2 / AXI 0.6.2 were never merged or used for stored artifacts; their envelope semantics are revised in place (no 0.5.3/0.6.3 inflation). Goldens regenerated and hand-verified against the formula.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions.</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>negative_power_sample</code> (negative rail power reaching the envelope/energy path breaks the monotonicity argument and refuses fail-closed) and <code>instrument_calibration_stale</code> (calibration artifacts now record capture wall time and a 24 h <code>max_age_s</code> validity horizon in protocol_v2; claim-time verification refuses missing/invalid capture time or age exceeded — a finite 40-pulse residual maximum is not an out-of-sample bound without recency enforcement). Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>capture_time_missing_or_invalid</code> (a v2 capture without a valid recorded capture wall time is invalid at minting, with the reason stated rather than silent). All only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception is retired with this entry. Replay purity note: the 0.5.1/0.6.1 arms keep their frozen binding expectation against the protocol_v2.json bytes current at their mint (<code>REPLAY_PROTOCOL_V2_SHA256</code>); custody-manifest verification and the staleness horizon are current-mint gates only.</li> <li><strong>Environment admission consumes the full evidence object.</strong> The shared validator fails closed on <code>critical_environment_passed</code>, <code>reference_provenance_present</code>, per-run evaluation eligibility, guard observations, and schema identity — and the post-run environment observation passes through the failure predicate on claim/whole-window paths (a post-run critical-environment failure refuses claim eligibility). This closes the Window-A screensaver contamination class end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>Calibration custody verified at claim time.</strong> The reducer enforces the validation-manifest reference: in-bundle containment, manifest hash, and presence + sha256 of every manifest member; any failure refuses as <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>. Current-era (0.5.2/0.6.2) claim-bearing use requires a protocol_v2 calibration artifact.</li> <li><strong>Collection floors.</strong> The 1.0 s post-window dwell minimum is enforced on every collection path (controller default, schema minimum, campaign-policy validation); sub-minimum configs refuse at validation. Scope spelling (delta-review adjudication): controller/CLI pre-collection rejection applies wherever powermetrics telemetry collects; mock-backend runs are not dwell-gated at the controller (mock telemetry cannot reach any claim path), while the campaign-policy schema minimum applies universally. Inner phase/item/block/level window entries carry the whole-trace anchor/calibration/tail barrier stamps whenever the top-level barrier fires.</li> <li><strong>Cooldown terminal-evidence normativity documented.</strong> The required terminal JSONL row fields (<code>release</code>, <code>release_criteria_met_late</code>), the cap-first precedence rule (&quot;the cap is causal and wins&quot;), and rejection semantics are contract text in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>, matching <code>joulewise/cooldown.py</code> exactly.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (third): provenance authentication rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after confirmation round 2 over <code>233e9e3</code> withheld sign-off (9 confirmed; the physics verified clean from every lens — all findings are provenance/governance). Rulings, implemented in the round-3 fix wave (frozen 0.5.1/0.6.1 replay semantics unchanged throughout):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declared facts are authenticated against primary bytes.</strong> The calibration&#39;s declared <code>capture_wall_time_s</code> must agree (±1 s) with the capture time independently derived from the hash-verified source events — a stale calibration can no longer be relabeled fresh (the P0).</li> <li><strong>Freshness covers the whole measurement.</strong> The 24 h horizon binds both <code>run_started</code> and the measured window END: <code>capture &lt;= run_started</code> and <code>window_end &lt;= capture + max_age_s</code>, inclusive. Pre-run delays cannot carry sampling past the declared validity of its calibration.</li> <li><strong>Version identity is validated generically.</strong> Generic bundle validation checks <code>reducer_version</code> against the closed known set and the §8.1 version/event-semantics pairing rules as a validation-time structured problem (no wire-schema enum — frozen-arm byte replay preserved); an unsupported <code>--reducer-version</code> yields the standard structured refusal, never a traceback.</li> <li><strong>Stored verdicts are re-derived, never trusted.</strong> The whole-window verifier rejects duplicated NEG-8 core members (occurrence-count semantics) and re-derives the bracket verdict from member evidence; disagreement with the stored row is <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Delta-review strengthening (lead ruling): the re-derivation tolerances come from the repo-REGISTERED campaign policy whose file hash matches the row&#39;s <code>policy_sha256</code> — the one trust anchor that does not terminate at bundle custody. Unknown policy hashes, and rows whose self-asserted tolerances disagree with the registered policy, refuse <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> before re-derivation. The custody boundary is otherwise explicit: a forger with bundle write access can rewrite row-internal hashes consistently, but cannot mint a matching tracked policy file.</li> <li><strong>Protocol identity is shape-authenticated.</strong> A v2 <code>protocol_id</code> requires the v2 estimator identity, capture/horizon fields, and v2 residual shape; v1-shaped bodies relabeled v2 refuse <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li><strong>Admission attempts have timing semantics.</strong> Attempt-ledger rows carry strictly increasing, non-overlapping declared windows on the strict path; violations refuse <code>environment_admission_missing</code>. 7a. <strong>(Fourth-wave addendum — claim-aggregation rulings, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 3 over <code>0925480</code> (instrument core verified defensible on fresh head collections by every lens; all four P0s in the claim-aggregation layer), the lead ruled: (1) floors/MDEs widen by EXACT linear-corner evaluation over member envelope intervals — residual widening <code>w_i·(n−1)/n + Σ_{j≠i}w_j/n</code>, contrast widening <code>Σ|c_i|·w_i</code> — never a max-width shortcut, and the dominance refusal fires against the widened quantity; (2) admission is causally bound to its run: the final attempt window ends at-or-before window start within <code>MAX_ADMISSION_GAP_S = 600</code> (inclusive), the post-run observation is captured at-or-after window end, and attempt windows must contain their stage&#39;s recorded idle-capture interval; (3) the whole-window verifier re-derives CPU admission and adapter continuity from member-bundle primary evidence, refuses nonempty condition lists and undecodable log lines (laundering must require consistent cross-bundle forgery, never a one-line edit — full erasure resistance inside bundle custody is impossible and is recorded as the honest boundary); (4) NEG-8 reference energies are re-reduced from primary evidence at the current mint at claim time (minutes-scale cost accepted), with canonical-workload identity (<code>canonical_neg8_workload</code> + <code>scientific_config_sha256</code> against the custody-bound config) enforced; (5) the four byte-frozen goldens carry executable sha256 pins. Round-4 confirmation follow-ups (same date): the universal <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code> barrier covers the <code>0.4.1</code>/<code>0.4.2</code> arms (every pre-repair wire, not only 0.5.0/0.6.0 — the former 0.4.x escape is closed and its test assertion inverted); the production trace-margin gate uses the full three-term composed bound including the wall-minus-monotonic span; campaign <code>ready_for_analysis</code> requires a registered claim-eligible mint (<code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code>; mock telemetry exempt — it can never bear claims). Recorded custody boundary: the 24 h calibration horizon compares host wall time, so an operator with host time control can evade it — accepted (host time integrity is an operator obligation, like bundle custody itself).</li> </ol> <p>7b. <strong>(Fifth-wave addendum — calibration epistemics, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 5 over <code>09b5de6</code> (the P0 was statistical, not mechanical: a 40-pulse sample maximum is not an out-of-sample deterministic bound — 87.1% confidence on the 95th percentile vs the D-054 doctrine&#39;s n=59 for 95/95), the lead ruled: (1) <strong>protocol_v3</strong> raises the pulse count to 59, satisfying the repo&#39;s own nonparametric 95/95 doctrine; v3 is required for future claim-bearing calibration captures (v2 artifacts stay verifiable as this arc&#39;s validation evidence). (2) <strong>B_fiducial&#39;s epistemic status is stated honestly everywhere</strong>: a 95/95 nonparametric calibration bound, deterministic for claims only under REGISTERED transfer assumptions — T1 binding-vector stationarity, T2 the authenticated 24 h horizon, T3 load-regime transfer (calibration pulses are GPU-matmul under CPU-light load; sustained mixed-load transfer is an assumption; a loaded-calibration protocol variant is the registered roadmap mitigation). (3) <strong>Calibration bracketing is required for claim-bearing collections</strong>: two valid artifacts bracketing the window (pre at-or-before start, post at-or-after end, each within its own horizon), consumed as <code>max(pre, post)</code>, refusing <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code> or on bracket drift beyond <code>calibration_bracket_max_drift_s</code> (production 10 ms). Single-calibration reduction remains valid only for non-claim-bearing probe/exploratory use. (4) <strong>Environment state is window-enforced</strong>: per-interval thermal-pressure records are scanned over the measured window (<code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> refusal); admission objects are recomputed from their embedded snapshots — a stored <code>eligible: true</code> is never trusted. (5) <strong>Loop-termination doctrine</strong>: convergence sign-off means zero UNADDRESSED P0/P1, where &quot;addressed&quot; includes a registered limitation with recorded justification, adjudicated by the lead. A physical instrument&#39;s uncertainty budget always rests on stated assumptions; the honest end state is registered assumptions, not infinite hardening. T3 is the first entry in that register. Round-6 follow-up (same date): the bracket maximum must be CONSUMED, not merely recorded — a claim refuses <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code> whenever <code>max(B_pre, B_post)</code> exceeds any member envelope&#39;s minted effective bound (the member must be re-reduced under the dominating calibration); the whole-window producer refuses duplicated member occurrences (occurrence-count doctrine at the producer, not just the claim verifier); the registered-policy trust anchor refuses duplicate-JSON-key policy bytes; and the standalone reducer horizon predicate upper-bounds <code>run_started</code> as well as the window end. Round-7 follow-ups (same date): the operative floor is the EXACT maximum of the complete D-054 guarded floor over the joint per-member interval corners (every component is convex in the member vector, so vertex enumeration is exact; n &lt;= 16 enumerated, larger widths refuse) — the linear-corner residual widening alone under-covered the Student-t prediction component; claim-licensing whole-window evidence requires the registered policy to be production-profile AND claim-bearing (exploratory rows can never license claims); the bracket-dominance gate authenticates each member&#39;s consumed bound from hash-verified calibration evidence (never the mint-time metadata scalar, whose disagreement is itself provenance-invalid); claim brackets accept protocol v3 artifacts ONLY (v2 stays valid as reduction/validation evidence). Round-8 follow-ups (2026-07-22): calibration identity is SEMANTICALLY authenticated, not just byte-authenticated — every calibration command event&#39;s two clocks (top-level <code>timestamp_s</code> and embedded ClockStamp epoch) must agree within 1 s on the strict path, and any event carrying a ClockStamp is skew-checked (the live artifact agrees within 0.205 ms; a shifted-freshness relabel now refuses); claim-time rederivation authenticates the EXECUTED v3 schedule (pulse durations, the deterministic van-der-Corput gap sequence within ±0.25 s, ≥4.5 s commanded-quiet baselines) so phase-locked or degenerate captures cannot claim the 95/95 identity; and the canonical floor/MDE artifact carries the corner-widened floor additively (validator recomputes it; the analysis engine consumes the WIDENED guarded floor as operative) — closing the honest-artifact-fails-closed gap so a sound end-to-end floor/MDE handoff exists. Registry additions for this wave: <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code>, <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code>, (claim-bearing window not bracketed by two authenticated, fresh calibration artifacts, or bracket drift beyond the registered tolerance) and <code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> (per-interval thermal-pressure records non-nominal — or missing on the strict path — anywhere in the admission-to-window span). Both only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception for them is retired with this entry.</p> <ol start="7"> <li><p><strong>Sign-off evidence must be head-minted.</strong> Any artifact or re-reduction quoted as validation evidence for a head must be regenerated AT that head (the pre-233e9e3 rederived calibration artifact lacks the horizon fields the head requires, and the probe re-reductions predate the strict calibration gates — both are re-minted at the final head before the sign-off record is written). Claim-bearing measurement additionally requires fresh live [QUIET-MAC] calibration under protocol v3 (59 pulses, fifth-wave addendum), bracketing the window, within 24 h of collection.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Confirmation round 9 (2026-07-22, FINAL under the Ed-ratified cap) — outcome and registered limitation L1.</strong> The round-9 review over head 040ca3a confirmed the fiducial chain, reduce-side verification taxonomy, and contract coherence clean, with ONE surviving blocker (CR9-1, repro-backed, lead-reproduced): the canonical floor/MDE artifact is SELF-ATTESTING about its admissible half-widths and campaign membership — <code>validate_floor_artifact</code> recomputes widened floors only from artifact-internal widths, and evidence binding authenticates identities, hashes, and ordering but neither rederives source widths nor requires complete governed campaign membership. A substituted artifact with understated widths (or one omitting a member) validates, binds, and licenses an exact claim floor. Per the loop-termination doctrine (clause 5), the lead adjudicates this a REGISTERED LIMITATION rather than a tenth round:</p> <ul> <li><strong>L1 (registered): canonical floor artifacts are not independently claim-licensing.</strong> Until floor↔extraction binding lands, a claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact ONLY when it was produced by the governed extraction in the same custody session as the analysis (same run manifest; extraction gates demonstrably executed). Standalone or externally supplied floor artifacts are non-claim-bearing evidence. Justification: the exposure is artifact substitution or a defective producer BETWEEN extraction and analysis; an honest same-session pipeline computes widths and membership under the already -hardened extraction gates, so no measurement this program will make under L1&#39;s workflow rule is affected. The gap is a third-party verifiability deficit, not an instrument-physics defect.</li> <li><strong>Queued fix (next cycle, P1):</strong> bind each canonical floor cell to its extraction report and source-member disposition (or rederive the extraction gates and widths at binding), refusing on any stored width/corner mismatch or membership deviation, with integration regressions for width substitution and member omission (TASK_QUEUE FLOOR-BIND-01). Round-9 verification note: the focused 357-test review surface passed at the head in-session; the lead&#39;s full-suite gate over the identical tree content (2088 passed / 15 skipped / 1570 subtests / 0 failures) stands as the aggregate confirmation.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>Live collection arc (2026-07-22/23) — collection-path regressions, occurrence supersession, and basis-scoped verdicts.</strong> The first live Window-A members after sign-off exposed collection-path defects invisible to nine review rounds without hardware; each was fixed under the ratified contracts (PR #80 canonical-attempt promotion + sole-sampler gapless design; PR #81 idle-slice cursor after forensics proved the slicer&#39;s own parsing contaminated the admission interval at the real ~120 ms powermetrics cadence). Two doctrine amendments were then ruled by the lead when the whole-window verdict path contradicted operational guidance (both defaults preserved, both overrides explicit and auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Occurrence supersession (amends the round-6 occurrence-count doctrine):</strong> duplicated member occurrences still REFUSE by default; a duplicate may resolve to the present bundle only when an explicit operator supersession artifact (append-only, hash-sealed, naming the superseded occurrence, quarantine destination, and reason — <code>--record-supersession</code>) exists; two present bundles always refuse.</li> <li><strong>Basis-scoped whole-window verdicts:</strong> latest-wins remains rejected (verdict-shopping prevention); every verdict records a canonical evaluation-basis hash (member occurrence set + calibration bracket set<ul> <li>policy) and binds only that basis; consumers match the claim&#39;s basis; legacy basis-less verdict rows never govern new claims. Diagnostic-cascade decoupling and whole-window waiver consumption landed in the same wave. Windows a5 (108 members) and prior attempts remain NON-claim-bearing as whole windows (true clock-anchor refusal on one member; NEG-8 end reference measured ~2 h post-collection failed the drift gate at 0.778 J — the instrument correctly refusing a stale bracket); their corpora stand as instrument-proving evidence. The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). def load_calibration_acceptance_bound(
    path: Path = DEFAULT_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_PATH,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Load the file-pinned D-102 acceptance artifact fail-closed."""

    try:
        raw = Path(path).read_bytes()
    except OSError:
        return None
    return _acceptance_bound_from_authenticated_bytes(raw)


def _acceptance_bound_from_authenticated_bytes(
    raw: bytes,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Parse acceptance bytes only when their role-indexed pin authenticates."""

    try:
        value = json.loads(raw)
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
    # Any file route is authenticated by one of the two reviewed exact-byte
    # states: the genesis fixture retained for pre-issuance tests, or the
    # deterministically emitted issued artifact. A caller cannot turn an
    # alternate self-consistent document into authority by choosing a path.
    expected_sha256 = {
        "schema_fixture_unissued": DEFAULT_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256,
        "issued": ISSUED_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256,
    }.get(value.get("artifact_role") if isinstance(value, Mapping) else None)
    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != expected_sha256:
        return None
    if not _valid_acceptance_bound(value):
        return None
    return dict(value)


def _authenticated_explicit_acceptance_bound(
    value: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Authenticate an in-memory artifact against the checked-in byte pin."""

    pinned = load_calibration_acceptance_bound()
    if pinned is None or dict(value) != pinned:
        return None
    return pinned


def _acceptance_artifact_sha256(artifact: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Return the reviewed exact-byte pin for a validated artifact role."""

    return (
        ISSUED_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256
        if artifact.get("artifact_role") == "issued"
        else DEFAULT_ACCEPTANCE_BOUND_SHA256
    )


def _valid_sha256(value: Any) -> bool:
    return (
        isinstance(value, str)
        and len(value) == 64
        and all(char in "0123456789abcdef" for char in value)
    )
